subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity performance validation & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jenny — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment.

Recap of inbound SLO/requirements (from the call):
- P95 tail latency target: <= 150 ms for streaming text generation (interactive flows, ~250-1024 token responses)
- Sustained throughput: 12k requests/day with burst to 2k reqs/min during peak events
- Concurrency: up to ~120 simultaneous streaming sessions during peak windows
- Streaming requirement: must support server-sent events (chunked tokens) with <=50ms inter-chunk latency for user-perceived responsiveness
- Model class: Llama-2-13B / Mistral-7B family (you mentioned pref for open models)

What we promised on the call:
1) High-level sizing recommendation (GPU family comparison + reserved throughput).
2) A short perf-validation run in your staging environment (2–4 hour window) to validate p95 latency and concurrency.
3) Provide a proposed canary config for Dedicated capacity and a short mutually-agreed MA plan.

Attachments: I’ve included our initial perf summary and your traffic CSV for reference.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm the sample traffic CSV we have attached is representative of peak traffic (Carlos: can you confirm?).
- Share preferred windows for a 2–4 hour perf validation (we can run Fri 4/16 or Mon 4/19).
- Confirm whether you want us to size for headroom (recommended) or strictly to target SLO.

I'll loop Marissa and Neha into the validation planning — they will lay out the GPU sizing and perf scripts.

Thanks,

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The traffic CSV we attached is a 24h sample of production traffic from last week. Peak minute had ~1,800 requests (we round to 2k for planning). Carlos can confirm the CSV is the canonical export.
- Most sessions are short (prompt + ~150 token reply) but about 15% are long-running streaming responses (400–1,000 tokens).
- We want to size with ~20% headroom over peak to avoid customer regressions during Black Friday-like spikes.
- Our preference is H100 if it materially reduces node count/cost, but we’re open to A100 if total cost + license is lower.

Available windows: Fri 2026-04-16 09:00–12:00 PT (preferred) or Mon 2026-04-19 13:00–17:00 PT. Let us know which works.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity performance validation & next steps

Hi Jenny — thanks for the details. Quick technical breakdown and our recommended starting configuration for the perf validation run. I’ll keep numbers conservative and we can adjust after the first run.

Assumptions:
- Model: Llama-2-13B (float16/quantized path)
- Typical response length: 150 tokens (85% of requests), long-tail 400–1,000 tokens (15%)
- Target: P95 <= 150ms observed at token granularity for streaming start + overall response within p95 target for short responses

GPU family comparison (rough expected perf for streaming token throughput and latency):
- H100 (1x node): ~1,800–2,200 tokens/sec sustained for the Llama-2-13B optimized runtime; better kernel fusion and nvlink bandwidth improves steady-state and long-stream latency.
- A100 (1x node): ~800–1,000 tokens/sec sustained for the same model in our tests; lower per-node throughput than H100.

Sizing guidance (to meet your peak with 20% headroom):
- Peak concurrent sessions: 120 sessions, avg throughput per session during active streaming = ~10 tokens/sec (conservative for interactive bursts). That’s ~1,200 tokens/sec sustained peak from active streams + background overhead.
- For mixed short/long responses and to keep p95 <=150ms: we recommend reserving ~2,500 tokens/sec capacity for the Dedicated pool.
  - Option A (H100s): 2x H100 nodes (reserve ~2 x 1,200 tok/s = ~2,400 tok/s) — provides headroom for spikes and reduces node count.
  - Option B (A100s): 3x A100 nodes (reserve ~3 x 850 tok/s = ~2,550 tok/s) — more nodes, similar capacity; may increase scheduling overhead.

Concurrency slots and autoscaling:
- Configure concurrency slots per node to 40 sessions/node for H100 (based on 120 session peak -> 3 slots x 40 each across 3 logical partitions) and 30 sessions/node for A100. Autoscale up to +1 node burst for 10–15 minute spikes.

Streaming latency controls:
- Enable prefix KV cache (your workload has repeated system prompts), set small emit buffer (<=32 tokens) for low inter-chunk latency, and use our low-latency kernel path for first-token delivery.

Perf validation plan (2–4h window):
1) We’ll run a staged load: 30% baseline -> 70% increased -> ramp to 100% peak (with 20% headroom).
2) Measure p50/p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end response latencies for short/long cases.
3) Verify streaming chunk inter-arrival <=50ms and overall p95 <=150ms.
4) Collect profiles and recommend final capacity commit.

Telemetry / credentials checklist we need from you:
- A staging endpoint (hostname) with access (mTLS cert or short-lived API key) — we prefer API key + IP allowlist for the run.
- A sanitized sampling of production traffic (you already attached CSV, good) and a small corpus of long-response prompts.
- Contact person on-call during the test (Carlos).

Next steps:
- Aditya: confirm the perf validation window (I can do Fri 4/16 09:00–12:00 PT).
- Jenny/Carlos: provide the staging endpoint creds and confirm the CSV is canonical.
- If validation looks good, we’ll produce an output-sizing doc (final recommended H100 vs A100 commit) and an MA plan for Dedicated rollout.

I’ve attached a short slide with the H100 vs A100 perf curves and a sample canary config.

—Marissa
